11.text: The houses of the deceased are said to be large round tents without

12.text: any seams, and shining like bubbles of saliva. Their reindeer-herds are nu-

13.text: merous, and consist of animals brought for sacrifice or slaughtered for meat,

14.text: and of wild reindeer killed in the hunt. Some of the inhabitants, however,

15.text: live by sea-pursuits on the shores of an ocean which abounds with walrus.

16.text: The men and the walrus play a kind of game in which the walrus pop up

17.text: out of the water, then dive again, while the men try to shoot them. When

18.text: an animal is shot, it is hauled ashore and eaten: then the bones are thrown

19.text: back into the water, and it comes to life again.

20.text: Some of the beliefs concerning the condition of the deceased in the

21.text: world beyond the grave seem to be contradictory. For instance, the assertion

22.text: that people, when they die, are killed by keˊlet or shamans, and their souls

23.text: are eaten by keˊlet, is hard to harmonize with the detailed description of the

24.text: life which different groups of the deceased lead in the other world.

26.text: believe, however, that these apparently contradictory ideas represent the feel-

27.text: ing of the Chukchee, from different points of view, toward death and the

29.text: the weight of the great sorrow, the Chukchee inclines to consider it a murder,

30.text: and tries to find out the one who caused the death, that he may place the

31.text: responsibility for it on men or spirits. When time has weakened the first

32.text: impression, he forgets the part the keˊlᴇ is supposed to have taken in the

33.text: death, and endeavors to picture to himself various features of the life the

34.text: deceased lead in their own dominions.

35.text: Another important seeming contradiction refers to the influence which

36.text: the deceased may have on the good or bad fortune of living human beings.

37.text: One line of native thought is inclined to consider the deceased as benevolent

38.text: protectors of their descendants. Some details in the arrangement of the

39.text: household charm-string¹ show elements of a real cult of ancestors.
